findings.message: Section 3 'Isolation' says each lane's session runs with a private TMPDIR, citing workflow/sessions.py:274-276 and workflow/interactive.py:143-152. Only print-mode ClaudeSessions.run (sessions.py:275-276) sets TMPDIR; InteractiveSessions.launch (interactive.py:145) passes the inherited environment with HERDR_* stripped and no TMPDIR, so the native sessions an automatic run launches share the system temp directory. Rated P2 because a per-lane temp directory is not a boundary the document relies on (the same paragraph's answer says nothing is a sandbox and workers have the account's shell), but the sentence should be scoped to print mode.

Section 3 'Worktrees after a run and stale registrations' says 'git worktree add at a registered path fails, which is how Partial candidate worktree exists and Interrupted check attempt exists surface'. Both messages come from explicit existence checks before any git command: pipeline.py:486 (cwd.exists()) and checks.py:152 (directory.exists()); git worktree add is never reached in those cases. The stale-registration reasoning (paths embed the run id) still holds, but the stated mechanism is wrong.
findings.requirement: what happens to worktrees after a run

findings.message: Section 3 'Isolation' ends with 'Tested:' naming SessionTests.test_exact_revision_and_distinct_worktrees, test_lock_and_dirty_worktree_fail_closed, PipelineTests.test_complete_offline_graph_with_real_browser_and_explicit_gates and InteractiveTests.test_reviewer_launch_requires_the_clean_candidate_worktree. None of them asserts the paragraph's first two claims: the refusal of a run directory inside the repository (sessions.py:189-190) and the 0700 run directory (sessions.py:191-192). No test in workflow/test_*.py mentions either (grep for 'outside the source repository' and '0o700' finds only executable chmods in fixtures). Those two should be marked untested like the symlink and changed-during-snapshot guards are.
findings.requirement: so every answer must cite where the behaviour is implemented

findings.message: Recommendation 3 (accept a completion file from a session that exited after writing it) rests on 'stop_session already handles an absent session'. It does not: Pipeline.stop_session (pipeline.py:334-336) raises '<node> session missing before stop; reconcile before continuing' when locate returns None and no stop marker exists, so freeze -> stop_workers would fail for exactly the lane the recommendation accepts. The recommendation also removes the only liveness binding section 5 describes for workers (file accepted only when the receipt's session is present and idle/done, automatic.py:121-136); with the launch token readable in plan.json, a file written mid-turn by a killed session, or by a sibling, would be accepted without any session check. The document should either name the stop_session change it requires or state that this weakens the identity binding rather than only reducing intervention.
findings.requirement: weakening an integrity boundary. Each names the file and function it changes and the test that would prove it.

findings.message: Recommendation 4's proving test ('interrupting after the first of two acceptances, removing that reviewer's inventory row, then resuming to an approved review.json') cannot pass without also relaxing check_independence (automatic.py:557-566), which _accept_native runs after wait_reviews (:578) and which raises 'Reviewer identity changed or is not independent' when any reviewer's row cannot be located (row is None). NativeReviewerTests.test_reviewer_missing_after_the_file_is_refused (test_automatic.py:989-998) asserts exactly that refusal. As written the recommendation either fails its own test or implies weakening the independence check, which the ranking criterion forbids; it should say which.
findings.requirement: weakening an integrity boundary. Each names the file and function it changes and the test that would prove it.

findings.message: Omitted escape in section 6 'Editing the run directory': the paragraph on a detached process left by a worker (surviving stop_session, pipeline.py:340-352) says it 'could rewrite evidence after the hashes were computed if it also rewrites the bundle and status files', but the cheaper move is to forge a reviewer verdict. Each reviewer's launch token is written to automatic-review-<id>.json (0600, same user) before the launch (automatic.py:509-513), read_review_completion binds the file only to run id, node id, that token, bundle digest and candidate commit (:313-315), and wait_reviews accepts it whenever the reviewer's row is idle or done (:363-365); nothing ties the file to the process that wrote it. A leftover process that reads the status file and rewrites <node>.completion.json with verdict approved inside the 2-second poll window after the real reviewer goes idle passes every check the document lists. It is the same same-user trust the runbook declares, but the section enumerates consequences per file and this one is missing.
findings.requirement: What can a worker execute and write, what can a reviewer execute and write

findings.message: Omitted escape in sections 3 and 6: every lane, verification, candidate and review worktree shares the source repository's .git, and the document lists 'reset the source branch' and 'delete refs or worktrees' but not the two persistent vectors that outlive stop_workers without a detached process. (1) Hooks: hooks are disabled only for the candidate cherry-pick (pipeline.py:492) and the integration merge (:564); git worktree add at checks.py:156, pipeline.py:488 and automatic.py:403 runs the repository's post-checkout hook, so a hook written into .git/hooks/ by a worker executes in the controller's process context at every later verification attempt and at review-worktree creation. (2) .git/info/exclude (per repository, shared by all worktrees) hides any path from git status --porcelain, which is the whole of the 'Source worktree is dirty' check (pipeline.py:554-555), the 'Reviewer worktree changed' check (automatic.py:579-580, 668-669) and the clean-start checks (sessions.py:204, checks.py:157, interactive.py:175, 224); the document says writes into the source checkout are 'detected as Source worktree is dirty at integration', which an excluded path defeats. Both belong in 'What a worker can do to another lane's tree or the source checkout'.
findings.requirement: stops a worker from committing, pushing, editing another lane's files or the run directory?

findings.message: pre-existing: the reviewer boundary ('no shell and one permitted write', section 6) depends on the candidate checkout carrying no project configuration the reviewer session would honour, and the controller's cleanliness checks cannot see such a file. The review worktree is the reviewer's cwd (interactive.py:221, 245), and Claude Code reads project settings and CLAUDE.md from the cwd; the repository's .gitignore ignores '*.local', so a .claude/settings.local.json dropped into review-worktree/ by any same-user process (for example a worker's leftover process) is invisible to git status --porcelain at interactive.py:224 and automatic.py:579-580/668-669, and the candidate commit itself may carry .claude/settings.json or CLAUDE.md only if a lane owns those paths. Whether --safe-mode disables project hooks is the open assumption the document already lists; until it is verified, 'Reviewer worktree changed' does not establish that the reviewer ran without project-injected hooks or instructions. The document's hostile-content paragraph considers only prompt injection through files the reviewer reads, not configuration the harness loads.
